notes.title: Fix for game crash on startup
notes.content:
Certain GPUs were causing the game to crash on startup. The shader compilation issue causing the crash has been fixed and the game should work as intended.

This may not fix the issue on every GPU. If you're still having a crash on startup problem, leave a message in the discussion area listing your PC specs and I can try to investigate further fixes.

- Owen

notes.title: Let's break the game with randomized mutators!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40372180/c5442adbf56fcab3445946e05731cc3cf167fe57.jpg[/img]

It's finally time to get the game into players hands and to celebrate I'm going to try to do everything I can to break the game in weird and (hopefully) interesting ways! I've added a mode that activates a random set of gameplay mutators each time a level starts.

I'll be playing through lots of areas that haven't been shown yet, so if you're looking for a sneak peek here's your chance. 

[h3][b]Human sized blender?[/b] It will be there. 
[b]Giant deadly CRT television?[/b] It will be there.
[b]Octopus costume?[/b] Yes, it will be there.[/h3]
[b]
Have an idea you'd like to see me attempt? Come by and drop your suggestions in the chat. [/b]

notes.title: Radio Viscera is about shoving enemies into traps with gleefully gory results
notes.content:
Everyone knows that kicking grunts intro traps in Dark Messiah of Might & Magic is one of the greatest pleasures in videogames. Radio Viscera looks like a game entirely about that feeling. Played from a top-down perspective, you wield an air cannon that can blast holes in walls and punt peeps into meat grinders.
